text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

CORN SALE - South Korean feed mill companies on Tuesday bought 52,500 tonnes of U.S. No.3 yellow corn from Japanese trading house Mitsubishi. The feed mill companies bought the corn at 87.95 cents per bushel over CBOT March futures if from the Pacific Northwest or at 85.95 cents over March if from U.S. Gulf. Shipment was set at seller's option for February 14-March 5 if from PNW or for Feb 1-20 if from the U.S. Gulf.

OAT SALE - South Korean feed mill companies, including Je il Feed Co Ltd, on Tuesday bought 1,500 tonnes of Canadian mixed feed oats at $117.50 a tonne on a C and F. Canadian exporter X-can Grain Pool Ltd sold the mixed feed oats through closed tender for shipment in December, the traders said.

RICE TENDER - The Japanese Food Agency said on Monday that it would buy 110,000 tonnes of rice at its import tender on October 24 and 10,000 tonnes at its November 8 tender. Under a 1993 General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade agreement, Japan agreed to gradually open its rice market and committed to import 511,000 tonnes of rice through March 1997.

WHEAT SALE - Algeria bought 50,000 tonnes Argentine wheat and 25,000 tonnes of French wheat Tuesday. One trader said Algeria bought two 25,000-tonne cargoes Argentine wheat for $165-$166 per tonne, c and f, Dec shipment. French wheat was for second half Nov shipment at $184 per tonne, c and f. Another source said the Argentine wheat was sold below $170 with freight. VEGOIL TENDER - Pakistan received three bids on Tuesday in response to its tender for 9,000 tonnes of RBD palm oil. Pan Century offered $505.40 per tonne FOB and Felda $508 per tonne FOB for 9,000 tonnes of palm oil first half November. Cargill offered $511.88 for 3,000 tonnes for shipment by November 20.

WHEAT TENDER - Algeria is seeking 75,000 extra tonnes of soft wheat of French and/or Argentine origin in three lots of 25,000 tonnes each, trading sources said. Shipments are set for November and December. The tender expires on Thursday.

WHEAT TENDER - Egypt's official commodities buyer said on Tuesday he was inviting bids for 50,000 tonnes of soft red French wheat or soft white standard wheat from Australia for delivery between November 1 and 15.

MARKET TALK - Moscow trade and agricultural sources shrugged off market talk that Russia was soon planning to import large quantities of North American or Australian wheat for its Far East, but did not rule out small purchases over a period. "We've been importing only soybeans, and we don't plan to buy any grain," said OGO President Arkady Zlochevsky. "It is nonsense to talk about any one company importing millions of tonnes for the Far East -- it's just rumours, a fairy tale."

... Argentine wheat traders said Monday that weekend frosts that hit the southern wheat belt may have caused significant damage to some crops in the area. But traders and analysts preached caution in assessing any damage and some said the cold snap might have hit too early in the crop's cycle to do much harm.

... Indian soymeal exporters have sold 575,000 tonnes of soymeal but offtake was limited due to fall in demand in foreign markets, traders said. They said soymeal yellow was quoted at $255 FAS (free alongside ship) for November shipments compared to $292-293 in mid-September.
